sketches: The paper states Conjecture 4.4 ({K2-digon, K_k, F} heroic for every oriented forest F) is equivalent to the special case H = TT_k of Conjecture 4.2, since forbidding the edgeless K_k in a digon-free digraph is interchangeable with forbidding TT_k (every tournament on 2^k vertices contains TT_k).

source.name: Heroic triple characterization via transitive tournaments
source.statement: Let $H$ be a hero and let $F$ be an oriented forest. The set $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2}, H, F\}$ is heroic if and only if: either $F$ is the disjoint union of oriented stars, or $H$ is a transitive tournament.
source.context: This is the main conjecture of the paper, a digraph analog of the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture for oriented graphs. The 'only if' direction is proved in Section 6.1. The case where both conditions hold simultaneously (H a transitive tournament and F a disjoint union of oriented stars) is already settled by Chudnovsky, Scott and Seymour [6].

target.name: Heroic triple with oriented forest and K_k
target.statement: Given an oriented forest $F$ and for every integer $k$, $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2}, K_k, F\}$ is heroic.
target.context: This conjecture is equivalent to the special case of Conjecture 4.2 where $H = TT_k$ is a transitive tournament, since every tournament on at least $2k$ vertices contains $TT_k$ as an induced subdigraph. It generalises the heroic-set result for $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2}, K_k, P^+(3)\}$ proved in Theorem 4.3, where $K_k$ denotes the digraph on $k$ vertices with no arc.

sketches: Oriented complete multipartite graphs contain no induced K1 + P-vec2 (an isolated vertex forces its non-neighbours into its own part, contradicting adjacency inside the path), so they form a subclass of {K1+P-vec2}-free digraphs. Hence if Delta(1,2,2) were a hero in {K1+P-vec2}-free digraphs it would be a hero in oriented complete multipartite graphs; the disproof of the latter (arXiv:2202.13306 v2) settles the former negatively.

Oriented complete multipartite digraphs contain no induced K_1 + P->_2 (disjoint union): a vertex nonadjacent to every vertex of the path must share a part with two adjacent path vertices, which lie in different parts. So oriented complete multipartite graphs form a subclass of {K_1+P->_2}-free digraphs, and 'Delta(1,2,2) is a hero' in the larger class restricts to the same statement on the subclass.

A digraph has no induced K_1 + P->_2 (arc plus isolated vertex) iff its underlying graph has no induced K_2 cup K_1, i.e. is complete multipartite. Oriented complete multipartite graphs are thus exactly the digon-free members of the {K_1+P->_2}-free digraphs, so heroism of Delta(1,2,2) in the larger class restricts to the oriented question.

source.name: Δ(1,2,2) hero status in {K₁+P⃗₂}-free digraphs
source.statement: Determine whether $\Delta(1,2,2)$ is a hero in $\{K_1 + \vec{P}_2\}$-free digraphs, i.e., whether $\{\Delta(1,2,2),\, K_1 + \vec{P}_2\}$ is $\vec{\chi}$-finite.
source.context: Theorem 1.11 (Aboulker, Aubian, Charbit) almost completely characterizes heroes in $\{K_1+\vec{P}_2\}$-free digraphs, and Theorem 1.12 of this paper extends the same structural characterization to $\{H, rK_1+\vec{P}_3\}$-free digraphs; in both settings the sole unresolved case is $H = \Delta(1,2,2)$.

target.name: Δ(1,2,2) hero in oriented complete multipartite graphs
target.statement: Is $\Delta(1,2,2)$ a hero in oriented complete multipartite graphs?
target.context: The paper characterizes heroes in oriented complete multipartite graphs up to the status of $\Delta(1,2,2)$. If the answer is no, heroes in oriented complete multipartite graphs are precisely those described in Theorem 1.3; if the answer is yes, a different complete characterization involving $\Delta(1,2,2)$ holds.

sketches: A k-extension adds k vertices one at a time; Conjecture 9 (unvd(D) <= C * unvd(D-v) for acyclic D) applied k times multiplies the unavoidability number by at most C^k, keeping it linear in |V| for each fixed k. The paper states Conjecture 11 'would follow from Conjecture 9'.

source.name: Bounded unvd ratio under vertex deletion
source.statement: There exists a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{unvd}(D)\leqslant C\cdot\operatorname{unvd}(D-v)$ for every acyclic digraph $D$ and for every vertex $v$ of $D$.
source.context: This conjecture generalizes Proposition 1, which gives $\operatorname{unvd}(D)\leqslant 2\operatorname{unvd}(D-x)$ only when $x$ is a source or sink of $D$, to arbitrary vertices. Together with Sumner's Conjecture 4, it implies Conjecture 10 about $k$-extensions of oriented trees.

target.name: k-extensions preserve linear unavoidability
target.statement: If $\cal F$ is linearly unavoidable, then the family of $k$-extensions of digraphs in $\cal F$ is also linearly unavoidable.
target.context: This conjecture, which would follow from Conjecture 9, asserts that the $k$-extension operation preserves linear unavoidability in general. The paper proves this for the specific family of oriented trees (and oriented forests) in Corollary 25.

sketches: Paper-stated conditional implication: Conjecture 9 (unvd(D) <= C*unvd(D-v)) applied to the k added vertices, TOGETHER with Sumner's conjecture (oriented trees of order n are (2n-2)-unavoidable), gives C^k(2n-2)-unavoidability of k-extensions of trees. Not standalone: it additionally needs Sumner's conjecture, which is outside this pair.

source.name: Bounded unvd ratio under vertex deletion
source.statement: There exists a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{unvd}(D)\leqslant C\cdot\operatorname{unvd}(D-v)$ for every acyclic digraph $D$ and for every vertex $v$ of $D$.
source.context: This conjecture generalizes Proposition 1, which gives $\operatorname{unvd}(D)\leqslant 2\operatorname{unvd}(D-x)$ only when $x$ is a source or sink of $D$, to arbitrary vertices. Together with Sumner's Conjecture 4, it implies Conjecture 10 about $k$-extensions of oriented trees.

target.name: Exponential unavoidability of tree k-extensions
target.statement: There is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every integer $k$, every $k$-extension of an oriented tree of order $n$ is $C^{k}(2n-2)$-unavoidable.
target.context: This conjecture is implied by Conjecture 9 (multiplicative stability under vertex addition) together with Sumner's Conjecture 4 (that oriented trees are $(2n-2)$-unavoidable). The paper proves a weaker result in Corollary 25, establishing $(2\cdot 3^{\binom{2k+2}{2}}\cdot|V(F)|)$-unavoidability for $k$-extensions of sufficiently large oriented trees.
